title: Interview · Mandatory Drills & Weak Claims
description: My rehearsed answers for experience-gap, leveling, tenure, and weak-claim interview questions — where I state my honest boundaries plainly, then pivot to the real depth I do have.

cards.front: Kubernetes vs. OpenShift — walk me through your container experience. (All 8 reqs name containerization; several name Kubernetes/Helm.)
cards.general: When a required tech spans a platform layer and hands-on work, separate what the platform did for you from what you personally wrote and ran. Draw the line explicitly so the interviewer trusts the rest of your answer, and keep it tight enough to leave room for follow-ups.
cards.specific: Short version: I state what I personally wrote and ran, then I draw the line between OpenShift's platform layer and the separate Kubernetes-native work I did, in under 90 seconds. My full drill card lives in 07-distributed-systems-and-observability.md.
cards.hint: Under 90 seconds; draw the platform-vs-native line explicitly.

cards.front: Walk me through your multi-agent system's graph topology. (Headline version.)
cards.general: For an architecture question, narrate the topology and the reasoning behind each node, not just the wiring. When you reach a mechanism you are not 100% sure of, state the true behavior you do know rather than guessing at exact internals — a confident wrong detail is worse than an honest boundary.
cards.specific: My LocalLLM's --multi flag: parallel researchers → analyst → critic, StateGraph fan-out/fan-in. In 60–90 seconds I cover why I used parallel researchers (coverage/redundancy, not just speed), how the analyst reconciles outputs, what the critic checks, and what happens on rejection — and I state the true retry-vs-annotate behavior; I don't guess if I'm unsure of the exact mechanism. My deep version is in 05-localllm-deep-dive.md.
cards.hint: 60–90s; don't guess the exact retry-vs-annotate mechanism — state what's true.

cards.front: Tell me about operating at scale — the 7M/day story.
cards.general: When telling a scale story, guard the number that is easy to misread. Pre-rehearse the one correcting sentence that keeps a latency or throughput figure from being heard as a claim about a different, more demanding path.
cards.specific: My 60-second scale narrative plus the ack-latency correction sentence I've rehearsed verbatim: the 10–20s p99 is peak async event-processing latency, never the sync front-door ack path. My full card is in 07-distributed-systems-and-observability.md.
cards.hint: The 10–20s p99 is async event-processing, not the sync ack path.

cards.front: Why no SageMaker / MLflow / edge tooling (ONNX, TensorRT)? (JPM-DigitalAuth)
cards.general: When asked about tooling you haven't used, answer with a plain 'none' and pivot immediately to the real, adjacent capabilities that do the same job. Never claim unused tooling — not even by implying adjacency or 'exposure' — because a single follow-up will expose it.
cards.specific: I'm honest: none — I haven't used SageMaker, MLflow, ONNX, or TensorRT. I pivot immediately to what's real for me: Terraform-provisioned AWS infra, containerized serving (my LocalLLM/FastAPI pattern), Kafka streaming. I never claim unused tooling, even adjacently.
cards.hint: Say 'none' first, then pivot to Terraform, containerized serving, Kafka.

cards.front: You've got 8+ years of experience — walk me through it. (JPM-BBAO)
cards.general: For an experience-gap question, state the true number plainly with no rounding up and no defensiveness, then let a concrete, verifiable body of work carry the weight the years don't. Naming the gap first buys credibility for everything you say after it.
cards.specific: The JD asks for 8+ years hands-on; my actual is ~5.8 years (5 yr 10 mo, computed, no gaps). I rehearse: I hold an M.S. in Data Science (UT Austin, conferred May 2026) plus a shipped, code-verified portfolio (LocalLLM, FedInsight, FrostByte, Project Overview). I state the gap plainly, then let my portfolio carry it. No defensiveness, no rounding up my years.
cards.hint: State ~5.8 years plainly, then let the portfolio carry it — never round up.

cards.front: This role is posted at a senior/lead level (SWES05). What level and comp are you targeting? (JPM-Senior Lead AI, JPM-PublicCloud)
cards.general: Decide your accept-level and comp floor before the first recruiter screen so it isn't decided live under pressure. Signal openness to a leveling conversation, lead with owned scope as your stretch case, and anchor against a down-level with the credential arc if one exists (a degree completed while doing the work). State your floor once and hold it.
cards.specific: I decide my accept-level and comp floor before the first recruiter screen — I don't let it get decided live. My posture: open to a leveling conversation; I lead with the scope I own (principal developer on the notification rebuild; FrostByte and Project Overview, both adopted by my team) as my stretch case; and I anchor against an SE III framing with the arc — SE II was my BS-commensurate level, and I completed my M.S. in Data Science (May 2026) while doing this work. I state my Lead/SWES04 floor once ($152–215K) and I hold it.
cards.hint: Floor once ($152–215K); scope leads; the MS anchors against SE III.

cards.front: Tell me about your experience managing and mentoring. (JPM-Lead ai-ml)
cards.general: When you lack a formal management title, open by naming that plainly and reframing toward influence, then give concrete, named examples of how you changed team practice. Specific instances beat an inflated title claim, which a follow-up would puncture.
cards.specific: I open with: "I haven't held a formal management title, so let me be specific about the influence I've had." Then I give three concrete, named examples, no title inflation: (1) my code-review ownership on the USAA team — what changed in team practice; (2) onboarding I built via the Project Overview VS Code extension; (3) my Ironhack-era peer tutoring.
cards.hint: Open by disclaiming the formal title, then give the three named examples.

cards.front: Walk me through a load or chaos test you've run. (JPM-FullStack-ai — binding-constraint role, extra weight.)
cards.general: When you lack direct evidence for a named requirement, say so cleanly and pivot to the closest real operational discipline you've actually practiced — the adjacent depth that shows the same skill under a different label.
cards.specific: I'm honest: I have no JMeter/Blazemeter/Chaos Monkey evidence; I pivot to the Kafka consumer-lag observability and SQS/Lambda backpressure work I did at USAA. My full card is in 07-distributed-systems-and-observability.md.
cards.hint: No load-test tooling evidence — pivot to Kafka lag and SQS/Lambda backpressure.

cards.front: Several of our reqs ask for 5+ years of GenAI/LLM work. How much do you have?
cards.general: For a tenure gap in a specialty, give the honest focused count and immediately frame it as sitting on top of a longer engineering foundation — position the depth of the base as the reason your specialty work is production-grade, not as an excuse for the shorter count.
cards.specific: Several reqs ask for 5+ years GenAI/LLM; my honest count is ~2 years of focused GenAI (LocalLLM, FedInsight, FrostByte, MS coursework) on top of 5.8 years of production engineering. My rehearsed line: "My focused GenAI/LLM work is about two years, but it sits on nearly six years of production engineering — the RAG system I've shipped is production-grade because of that foundation."
cards.hint: ~2 years focused GenAI on ~6 years production engineering — that base is why it's production-grade.

cards.front: Why is a Software Engineer II applying for a Lead / Senior-Lead role?
cards.general: When your title lags your scope, give the jump a cause: open with the arc (hired at the level commensurate with your old credential; completed the new degree while doing the work), cite the concrete scope that proves it, and stay open to a leveling conversation rather than insisting on a title match. Openness reads as confidence.
cards.specific: The arc: SE II is the level I was hired at with a bachelor's. Since then I completed an M.S. in Data Science (UT Austin, May 2026, GPA 3.97) while serving as principal developer on the notification rebuild and shipping two AI tools my team adopted — FrostByte and Project Overview. The work demonstrated the scope; the degree formalized the AI/ML depth — this loop is about the level commensurate with both. I stay open to a leveling conversation, not insisting on a title match.
cards.hint: Arc: BS→SE II; MS (May 2026) + demonstrated scope → next level; open to leveling.

cards.front: Tell me about the hybrid search / reranking you built in FedInsight. (Guardrail card.)
cards.general: For work that is real but unpublished, hold a firm boundary: it's fair to mention as recent engineering, but do not claim it's published or cite numbers from it unless specifically pushed. Know exactly where the line is before you're in the room so you don't drift over it under enthusiasm.
cards.specific: I built it code-complete and tested it locally only — I haven't pushed it to the public repo, and it's not on any resume. If retrieval depth comes up, it's fair for me to mention it as recent engineering work; I do NOT claim it's published or cite numbers from it unless I'm pushed on the point. My deep technical version of what I actually built lives in 06-fedinsight-deep-dive.md.
cards.hint: Local-only, not published — mention as recent work, no numbers unless pushed.

cards.front: If pressed on the RAG-prototype line from one of the two already-sent resumes (VP-FullStack, Lead SWE Firmwide) — what's the rehearsed bridge, and when do I use it?
cards.general: New materials never mention the internal RAG prototype at all — this isn't a claim to defend in general, it's context-specific insurance for two already-sent resumes that predate the current no-RAG-prototype directive. If asked, state the honest boundary plainly: it was prototyped, not selected for deployment, then pivot immediately to the shipped work. Never volunteer this unprompted in any other screen, and never imply the prototype had production traffic or usage numbers to quote.
cards.specific: For the two already-sent resumes only (VP-FullStack req 210750779, JPM Lead SWE Firmwide req 210767095): "I prototyped a RAG service at work end-to-end; it wasn't selected for deployment. FedInsight is my shipped RAG work — I designed and built it on my own time, and it's live and public. I designed the eval methodology for it and I'm building the harness now." I never volunteer this in any other screen, and I never imply the prototype was in production or had QPS/user numbers.
cards.hint: Two screens only — prototyped, not selected for deployment, then pivot to FedInsight. Never volunteer elsewhere.

cards.front: Push again on your Kubernetes-distinct work — where exactly did that happen?
cards.general: A claim that survives one telling but collapses on the second follow-up is worse than a narrower claim you can defend indefinitely. Rehearse the deeper layer so the distinction holds under repeated probing.
cards.specific: My Kubernetes-distinct-work claim must not collapse under a second follow-up — I keep my full drill in 07-distributed-systems-and-observability.md.
cards.hint: Must survive the second follow-up, not just the first.

cards.front: Describe your observability and multi-cloud stack (Dynatrace, Azure/GCP). (Firmwide gap 7.3a)
cards.general: For a multi-cloud/tooling requirement you only partly meet, never claim the tools or cloud depth you lack. Volunteer your true-today stack unprompted, framing it as the same discipline over a narrower footprint — proactively naming the boundary early in a screen is stronger than being caught by it later.
cards.specific: I never claim Dynatrace, or Azure/GCP hands-on depth. My rehearsed pivot: OpenTelemetry + Prometheus + Kafka event-lifecycle state tracking + CloudWatch monitoring + DLQ/retry handling on the USAA notification-platform rebuild is my true-today observability stack — same discipline (turning raw signal into actionable state), narrower cloud footprint (AWS-only). I say this unprompted if the multi-cloud or observability-stack requirement comes up early in a screen.
cards.hint: No Dynatrace/Azure/GCP claim; volunteer the AWS-only OTel/Prometheus/CloudWatch stack unprompted.

cards.front: How much multi-cloud (Azure/GCP) experience do you have?
cards.general: When one cloud is deep and others aren't, answer at the level of portable architectural primitives that transfer across clouds rather than claiming hands-on fluency you don't have. Never upgrade 'exposure' into 'expertise.'
cards.specific: My AWS is deep and production-proven; my Azure/GCP are not. I answer at the level of portable architectural primitives (structured logging, correlation IDs, common event schemas) that would transfer across clouds, rather than claiming hands-on Azure/GCP fluency I don't have. I never overclaim my "exposure" as "expertise."
cards.hint: AWS deep; Azure/GCP via portable primitives only — never 'exposure' as 'expertise.'

cards.front: Do you have ServiceNow / Jira Service Management and config-management (Ansible/Chef/Puppet) experience?
cards.general: For a structural tooling gap, honesty informs strategy rather than needing a defensive drill: acknowledge the gap plainly and pivot to the genuinely adjacent skill, naming it as a fast ramp-up rather than papering over a hidden gap.
cards.specific: I have no ServiceNow/Jira Service Management integration experience to evidence, and no Ansible/Chef/Puppet config-management experience. I pivot to my webhook/API integration experience (FastMCP tool exposure, LangGraph tool-calling) as the adjacent skill, and I name it as a fast ramp-up rather than a hidden gap.
cards.hint: Acknowledge the gap; pivot to webhook/API integration (FastMCP, LangGraph) as a fast ramp-up.
